pool.text: Pyotr Beketov established the Lensky Ostrog on the banks of the Lena River.
The fort survived a siege carried out by the local Yakuts.
The fort became the central administration of the newly formed Yakutsk Voivodeship.
The Holy Trinity Cathedral was constructed in Yakutsk.
Yakutsk officially received city status under that specific name.
A theological seminary opened at the request of Ilya Shadrin in Yakutsk.
The seminary transformed into the Yakutsk Theological School.
Yakutsk attained the official designation of a regional city.
An imperial decree established a separate Yakutsk-Vilyuysk Diocese centered in Yakutsk.
The Holy Trinity Cathedral closed due to Soviet religious policy.
The Melnikov Permafrost Institute was founded to solve building problems on frozen soil.
A conflict occurred at Lake Tyoploye which later engulfed Yakutsk.
The previously abolished local diocese was successfully restored.
Catholic priests belonging to the Salesians of Don Bosco began missions.
The Roman Catholic Church of the Holy Trinity opened in Yakutia.
The reconstruction of Yakutsk Airport transformed it into a modern international complex.
The Gagarin Center for Culture and Contemporary Art opened in Yakutsk.
The population of Yakutsk reached 355,443 residents at the census.
A corpus of written documents including birch bark letters was discovered in Yakutsk.
A historical paper letter-appeal addressed to Archimandrite Feofan was found.
